SMTO-LLM-0026 — The model server couldn't arrange the conversation for its model

GUID: 2ebf3119-546f-4f23-8f39-917f2c76c6fe
Slug: chat-template-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model server turned the request down with a message about its chat format, the layout its model expects conversations in. The exact cause isn't confirmed, and nothing from this request was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. If this small test also fails, the problem is in the server's setup for this model, not in your task.
  2. Send the copied error details to the person who manages the model server and ask them to check the server's chat format for this model. Each model needs a matching chat format on the server, and SMTO can't change that setting.
  3. After they confirm a fix, select Check saved model again, then on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The rejected request did nothing, so continuing is safe once the server accepts requests.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • If the server can't be fixed soon, choose another model on the Main card, select Save Main, and start the remaining work as a new task, after checking what the stopped task already finished. Don't install extra software until the cause is confirmed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider rejected the request (HTTP 400/422) and its error text matched chat-template markers such as 'chat template', 'unexpected message role' or 'system message must be at the beginning' (chat_template_rejected).

What this means

  • The rejection classifier found wording associated with the chat template. This narrows the next check but does not prove the provider’s exact internal failure. Check the recorded status and serving configuration before changing the request or installing components.

Why this can happen

  • Provider diagnostic text matched the chat template category. The exact rejected feature still needs confirmation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare supported message roles and ordering with the configured serving template.
  • Have the provider operator reproduce the specific rejection with a small sanitized test, without sharing the original prompt or tool arguments.

How to fix it

  • Check http_status and any message_roles in provider_diagnostic, then compare the request's role order with the serving chat template (for example vLLM's --chat-template or the model's bundled template). Correct the confirmed incompatibility on the server, verify with a small native tool-call request, then resume; the category comes from provider text markers and is not proof of the exact cause.
  • Compare supported message roles and ordering with the configured serving template. Ask the provider operator to correct the confirmed incompatibility before another Agent decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts a controlled request using the required native tool format.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The category is selected by bounded provider-text markers, not authoritative structured root-cause evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
